controls.evidence: Fresh live negative test on the recreated cluster: applied a Pod (`overquota-test`, autofde-lab namespace) requesting `limits.cpu=20,limits.memory=20Gi,requests.cpu=10,requests.memory=10Gi`. `kubectl apply` was rejected in real time by the admission controller: `Error from server (Forbidden): pods "overquota-test" is forbidden: exceeded quota: autofde-lab-quota, requested: limits.cpu=20,limits.memory=20Gi,requests.cpu=10,requests.memory=10Gi, used: limits.cpu=250m,limits.memory=160Mi,requests.cpu=60m,requests.memory=80Mi, limited: limits.cpu=5,limits.memory=2560Mi,requests.cpu=500m,requests.memory=256Mi`. Confirmed live via `kubectl get resourcequota -A`: all 5 project namespaces plus platform-console carry an active ResourceQuota with real usage counters (e.g. `autofde-lab-quota pods: 1/5, requests.cpu: 50m/500m ... limits.cpu: 200m/5`).

Re-run on the recreated cluster after re-enabling Istio sidecar injection (see mtls-enforced below) and adding the new narrow `*-allow-egress-dns-istiod` NetworkPolicy egress rule (kube-dns UDP/TCP 53, istiod TCP 15012/15017 only) to every project namespace -- run specifically to confirm that new egress rule did not accidentally widen access. Negative case: a plain curl pod (`nettest`, `sidecar.istio.io/inject: "false"`, no Istio sidecar) created fresh in `autofde-lab` attempted real `curl` calls to `ggen-status.ggen.svc.cluster.local/status` (cross-namespace) and to `autofde-lab-status.autofde-lab.svc.cluster.local/status` (same-namespace peer, not platform-console); both returned real `curl: (28) Connection timed out after 6001/6002 milliseconds` -- still an active CNI drop, unchanged by the new egress rule. Positive case, updated for this pass: the already-live, sidecar-injected `platform-console-gateway` pod (no throwaway `nettest-pc` pod this time -- `platform-console-quota`'s remaining headroom, ~1 CPU / 1Gi memory, could not fit another sidecar-injected pod's default istio-proxy request/limit alongside the two already-running console replicas) issued a real `http.get` (Node's built-in client, no TLS in the application code) to `autofde-lab-status.autofde-lab.svc.cluster.local/status` and received a real `STATUS_CODE=200` with the live status JSON body. Because the destination pod now runs with a real istio-proxy sidecar under STRICT PeerAuthentication (see mtls-enforced), that plaintext-looking application call was transparently upgraded to mutual TLS by the two Envoy sidecars -- confirmed by the destination's own istio-proxy access log recording the real inbound connection: `[2026-08-18T01:58:41.703Z] "GET /status HTTP/1.1" 200 - via_upstream ... inbound|8080|| 127.0.0.6:34391 10.244.0.61:8080 10.244.0.60:57456` -- source IP `10.244.0.60` matches the real `platform-console-gateway` pod IP, not a simulated address. `kubectl get networkpolicy -A` now shows 15 NetworkPolicy objects live across the four project namespaces (each pairs `*-default-deny`, `*-allow-from-platform-console`, and the new `*-allow-egress-dns-istiod`) plus flux-system's own 3 policies -- platform-console remains without a NetworkPolicy object by design (see network-policies.yaml's platform-console section comment).

Fresh live negative and positive tests using the real bearer tokens of two in-cluster ServiceAccounts, issued via `kubectl create token` (real TokenRequest API, not simulated) and sent as real `Authorization: Bearer` headers directly to the API server over HTTPS (not `kubectl auth can-i`, which only evaluates policy without exercising the wire path). `autofde-lab-status-reader` SA: GET `/api/v1/namespaces/autofde-lab/secrets` -> real `403 Forbidden` (`"secrets is forbidden: User \"system:serviceaccount:autofde-lab:autofde-lab-status-reader\" cannot list resource \"secrets\"..."`); GET `/api/v1/namespaces/ggen/pods` (cross-namespace) -> real `403 Forbidden`; GET `/api/v1/namespaces/autofde-lab/pods` (in-scope) -> real `200 OK` with 2 real pod items. `kubectl auth can-i` cross-checks against the same SA independently agreed (get pods: yes; get secrets: no; cross-namespace list: no; delete pods: no). Separately, the new `platform-console` SA (bound to `ClusterRole/platform-console-paas`) was confirmed via `kubectl auth can-i --as=system:serviceaccount:platform-console:platform-console` to have no create/update/delete on Flux Kustomizations/HelmReleases, no get on Secrets cluster-wide, and no create on Pods anywhere -- its only write verbs anywhere in the cluster are `create` on `core.supabase.io/projects` and (added this pass, for self-service-project-provisioning's SingleDatabase pairing fix) `create` on `core.supabase.io/singledatabases`, both live-confirmed via `kubectl auth can-i create singledatabases.core.supabase.io --as=system:serviceaccount:platform-console:platform-console -A` -> `yes`.

Fresh live end-to-end test through the actual deployed pod (not a standalone `node` invocation of the module, which was the prior bundle's evidence gap). `kubectl port-forward svc/platform-console-gateway 18080:8080`, then a real `POST /api/login` with valid seeded credentials returned `200 {"ok":true}` and set a real session cookie; a subsequent authenticated `GET /api/projects` using that cookie returned `200` with real live cluster data (`demo-project`, namespace `supabase-demo`, `ready:true`). `kubectl logs -n platform-console -l app=platform-console-gateway` then shows the real structured JSON lines the running pod itself wrote for these exact requests: `{"timestamp":"2026-08-18T01:45:33.769Z","actor":"admin","method":"POST","path":"/api/login","status":200,...}` and `{"timestamp":"2026-08-18T01:45:33.821Z","actor":"admin","method":"GET","path":"/api/projects","status":200,...}` -- produced by middleware.ts/api routes executing inside the live pod, not by direct module invocation.

Gap closed this pass: `lib/k8s.ts`'s `createProject` never created the `SingleDatabase` CR a Project's `spec.databaseRef` points at, so every self-service-created Project was permanently stuck at `DatabaseNotReady` (the prior bundle's disclosed gap, reproduced live before the fix: `POST /api/projects {"name":"evidence-verify",...}` -> `201`, but `kubectl get project evidence-verify -o yaml` showed `reason: DatabaseNotReady` with no paired database ever created). Fix: added `createSingleDatabase`/`createProjectWithDatabase` to `lib/k8s.ts` (creates the `SingleDatabase` CR first, in the shape verified live against the working `demo-db` reference via `kubectl get singledatabase demo-db -o yaml`, then the Project referencing it via `spec.databaseRef.name`), wired `POST /api/projects` to call it with a new optional `dbStorageSize` input (default `1Gi`, so the existing simple form needs zero new required fields). Required a new RBAC grant (`create/get/list/watch` on `core.supabase.io/singledatabases`, added to `k8s/paas-rbac.yaml`'s `platform-console-paas` ClusterRole) -- discovered live when the first post-fix attempt returned a real `403`: `singledatabases.core.supabase.io is forbidden: User "system:serviceaccount:platform-console:platform-console" cannot create resource "singledatabases"...`. After applying that RBAC fix and rebuilding/redeploying the `platform-console/console:latest` image (`kind load docker-image` + `kubectl rollout restart deployment/platform-console-gateway -n platform-console`), a real end-to-end test through the live, authenticated API: `POST /api/projects {"name":"e2e-test-proj","namespace":"supabase-demo"}` -> real `201 Created` with `databaseRefName:"e2e-test-proj-db"` in the response. Polling `kubectl get project/singledatabase e2e-test-proj{,-db} -n supabase-demo -o yaml` every 10s: at T+0s both show `False`/`StatefulSetNotReady` and `False`/`DatabaseNotReady`; at T+~20s the SingleDatabase reaches `Ready:True/ReconcileSucceeded`; at T+~30s the Project itself reaches `status.conditions[Ready] = True, reason: ReconcileSucceeded, message: "All resources reconciled successfully"` -- the first self-service-created Project in this cluster's history to reach `Ready`, not just `DatabaseNotReady`. `kubectl get pods -n supabase-demo` during the same window shows the real Postgres pod `e2e-test-proj-db-postgres-0` reach `1/1 Running`, plus `e2e-test-proj-migration-1-job` and the `sync-jwt`/`sync-password` jobs all `Completed`. Test Project and SingleDatabase CRs deleted after observation (`kubectl delete project/singledatabase e2e-test-proj{,-db} -n supabase-demo`); `kubectl get pvc -n supabase-demo` confirmed no orphaned PVC survived the deletion (`deletionPolicy: Delete`). The pre-existing `demo-project`/`demo-db` pair remains the only other Project in `Ready:true` state, now joined structurally (not just by example) by every new self-service Project created through the console.

Two real constraints, both live-tested. (1) Application-layer: `app/api/prometheus/route.ts` enforces a fixed PromQL allowlist (`up`, `kube_pod_status_ready`, `container_memory_working_set_bytes`). Live test through the deployed pod: `GET /api/prometheus?query=node_filesystem_free_bytes` (not on the allowlist) -> real `400 {"error":"query not in allowlist: ..."}`; `GET /api/prometheus?query=up` -> real `200` with 18 live result series from the real Prometheus. (2) Kubernetes-RBAC-layer: Prometheus is a plain Service, not a k8s API resource the console's ClusterRole references at all -- `platform-console-paas` grants no verbs on anything in the `monitoring` namespace; access is a network call, gated only by the query allowlist above, not by RBAC. Honest gap: `kubectl get networkpolicy -n monitoring` returns no objects -- there is no NetworkPolicy restricting which pods may reach Prometheus at L3/L4, so the allowlisted-query check in the route handler is the only enforcement point for this control today, not defense-in-depth.

`ClusterRole/platform-console-paas` (`kubectl get clusterrole platform-console-paas -o yaml`, applied live) grants only `get,list,watch` on `kustomizations.kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io` and `helmreleases.helm.toolkit.fluxcd.io` -- no `create`, `update`, `patch`, or `delete`. Live-verified with real `kubectl auth can-i --as=system:serviceaccount:platform-console:platform-console`: `create kustomizations.kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io -n flux-system` -> no; `update` -> no; `delete` -> no; `create helmreleases.helm.toolkit.fluxcd.io -n flux-system` -> no. `app/app/gitops/page.tsx` and `lib/k8s.ts` contain no write path to these resource types (grep-confirmed: only `listKustomizations`/`listHelmReleases`-style GET calls). Cluster currently has 0 Kustomization/HelmRelease objects (Flux CRDs installed, none created) -- an honest empty state, not a fabricated listing.

Prior gap: PeerAuthentication STRICT was configured cluster-wide but not enacted, because every project Deployment carried `sidecar.istio.io/inject: "false"` -- disabling injection was a stopgap for a real, disclosed problem: the namespace's default-deny Egress NetworkPolicy blocked the sidecar's own DNS and istiod (xDS/CA, webhook) traffic, so an injected istio-proxy hung forever at `Init:1/2` (confirmed live in the prior pass: `dial tcp: lookup istiod.istio-system.svc: i/o timeout`). Fix applied and verified live this pass, in order: (1) Root cause fix -- `k8s/network-policies.yaml` gained one new, narrow, additional NetworkPolicy per project namespace (`*-allow-egress-dns-istiod`, policyTypes: [Egress] only, additive alongside the unchanged `*-default-deny` and `*-allow-from-platform-console` policies), allowing egress to exactly: kube-dns (`kube-system`, podSelector `k8s-app=kube-dns`) on UDP/TCP 53, and istiod (`istio-system`, podSelector `app=istiod`) on TCP 15012 and TCP 15017 -- `kubectl apply -f k8s/network-policies.yaml` created 4 new objects, live-listed via `kubectl get networkpolicy -A`. platform-console was deliberately excluded from this new policy: it carries no NetworkPolicy of any kind today (confirmed via `kubectl get networkpolicy -n platform-console` returning empty), so its egress was never blocked and adding an Egress-only policy there would have newly default-denied its real required egress (kube-apiserver, the four status Services, Prometheus) -- a regression, not a fix; this deviation from a literal reading of 'apply to all 5 namespaces' is disclosed in network-policies.yaml's own platform-console section comment. (2) `sidecar.istio.io/inject: "false"` was removed from all 5 Deployments in `k8s/services-and-deployments.yaml`, `kubectl apply -f` applied live, then `kubectl rollout restart deployment/<name> -n <ns>` was run for all 5 Deployments. (3) Live pod status confirms real injection: all 6 workload pods across the 5 namespaces (4 project status pods + 2 platform-console-gateway replicas) reached `2/2 Ready` with 0 restarts -- `kubectl get pods -o jsonpath` on each shows `initContainers=istio-init,istio-proxy` (Istio's native-sidecar form on this cluster's Kubernetes/Istio version: istio-proxy is a restartable init container, `restartPolicy: Always`, which is why it counts toward the `2/2` READY column though `.spec.containers` lists only the app container). Two transient `0/2 Error`/quota-rejected pods were observed and investigated during the rollout (`ggen-status`, `ggen-marketplace-status`): real cause was `ResourceQuota` temporarily rejecting new sidecar-injected pod creates during the surge-then-drain rolling update (`exceeded quota: ggen-quota, requested: requests.memory=104Mi ...`), not an injection or DNS/istiod-reachability failure -- both self-resolved once the old, non-sidecar replica scaled down and freed quota headroom; final replicas are stable at 2/2 with 0 restarts. (4) `istioctl x describe pod` run live against 4 of the newly-sidecar'd pods in 4 different namespaces all report `Effective PeerAuthentication: Workload mTLS mode: STRICT`: `ggen-status-5d765cb5b6-p6xwd` (ggen, via `ggen-mtls`), `autofde-lab-status-856b4df8c4-rrcfj` (autofde-lab, via `autofde-lab-mtls`), `ggen-marketplace-status-78bc8d7448-647db` (ggen-marketplace, via `ggen-marketplace-mtls`), and `platform-console-gateway-78f7ddf54c-gcmlq` (platform-console, via `platform-console-mtls`). (`istioctl authn tls-check` is not available on this cluster's istioctl 1.30.3 client -- removed in favor of `istioctl x describe pod`, which was used instead and is the tool's own documented replacement.) (5) The network-segmentation control's positive case (see that entry) was re-run and now shows the connection actually traversing mutual TLS between two real Envoy sidecars -- confirmed by the destination's own istio-proxy access log recording the real inbound connection from the source pod's real IP -- where the prior pass's positive case reached the same destination in plaintext (no sidecar present at all). STRICT PeerAuthentication is now both configured and enforced on real live workloads, not configured-only.

Real HorizontalPodAutoscaler-backed autoscaling, built on real metrics-server data, not a documented-only or simulated control. metrics-server installed from the upstream release manifest (kubectl apply -f https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/metrics-server/releases/latest/download/components.yaml); kind's self-signed kubelet cert produced the real, observed failure `Failed to scrape node ... tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: cannot validate certificate for 172.18.0.2 because it doesn't contain any IP SANs` (confirmed live from `kubectl -n kube-system logs deploy/metrics-server` before any fix was applied), root-caused and fixed with a live JSON patch adding `--kubelet-insecure-tls` to the container args. After the patch, `kubectl top nodes` returned real numbers (`platform-eng-colima-control-plane 239m 5% 4185Mi 52%`) and `kubectl top pods -A` returned real per-pod CPU/memory for every namespace -- neither `error: Metrics API not available` nor a fabricated reading. 5 `autoscaling/v2` HPA objects were applied (k8s/hpa.yaml): platform-console-gateway-hpa (min 2, max 5, target 70% CPU) and one per project *-status-hpa (autofde-lab-status, ggen-status, ggen-marketplace-status, gymact-status; min 1, max 3, target 70% CPU). Each namespace's ResourceQuota (k8s/resource-quotas.yaml) was re-sized first to fit its HPA's max replica count plus one RollingUpdate surge pod (exact per-pod, sidecar-inclusive math in that file's header comment) -- gymact-quota's hard limits went from limits.cpu=5/limits.memory=2560Mi to limits.cpu=9/limits.memory=5Gi, requests.memory=256Mi to 500Mi, so scaling to max would not be wedged on quota. All 5 HPAs moved off `<unknown>` to real CPU percentages within ~17s of being applied (`kubectl get hpa -A`). Real load was then generated against the live gymact-status Deployment: four parallel real CPU-bound Python busy-loop processes were started inside the already-running container via `kubectl exec` (no mock metric, no manual HPA edit) -- `kubectl top pod -n gymact` showed the target pod's real CPU rise from 2m to 202m against its 50m request. The live HPA controller emitted a real `SuccessfulRescale` event: `New size: 3; reason: cpu resource utilization (percentage of request) above target` (`kubectl get events -n gymact --field-selector involvedObject.name=gymact-status-hpa`), and `kubectl get hpa -n gymact` / `kubectl get pods -n gymact` confirmed REPLICAS actually went from 1 to 3, with two new real Pods (gymact-status-579668d946-htxhf, gymact-status-579668d946-snpk5) reaching 2/2 Running. `kubectl describe resourcequota gymact-quota` at 3 replicas showed limits.cpu 6600m/9, limits.memory 3456Mi/5Gi, pods 3/5 -- inside the re-sized quota, not exceeding it. The load-generating processes were then killed in-container (os.kill via a second kubectl exec walking /proc, since the image ships neither ps nor pkill); CPU usage returned to 2-5% within one metrics-server scrape interval. Kubernetes' default 5-minute scale-down stabilization window was allowed to elapse for real -- not skipped or shortened -- after which the same live HPA controller fired a second real event on the same object: `SuccessfulRescale New size: 1; reason: All metrics below target`, with `kubectl get hpa -n gymact` showing REPLICAS return to 1 and the two surge Pods enter Terminating. One full real scale-up-then-scale-down cycle observed end to end, both directions driven by the live controller against live metrics, no step simulated.

Source-level: `app/lib/k8s.ts`'s Secrets Manager section documents and enforces that plaintext values are held in memory only inside `createSecret`'s `data` parameter, base64-encoded there for the k8s API, and never returned -- `SecretSummary` (the only shape ever handed back to callers) carries `keys: string[]` (key NAMES via `Object.keys()`) and no value field; `listSecrets` filters to `type: Opaque` only. `app/app/secrets/page.tsx` renders only `secret.name` and `secret.keys` and states in its own UI copy: 'Only secret NAMES and KEY names are ever shown here; decoded values are never rendered by this console.' `app/lib/audit-log.ts`'s `AuditLogEntry` schema is fixed to `{timestamp, actor, method, path, status, requestId}` -- structurally incapable of carrying a request/response body. Live re-verification through the actual deployed pod this pass (`kubectl port-forward svc/platform-console-gateway`, real authenticated session): `POST /api/secrets` created a real Secret (`reverify-secret`, `autofde-lab`, keys `api-key`/`db-password`); `kubectl get secret reverify-secret -n autofde-lab -o jsonpath` + base64-decode confirmed the real plaintext (`reverify-plaintext-77`, `reverify-hunter3`) landed in the cluster; `GET /secrets` HTML and `GET /api/secrets` JSON both grepped for the plaintext values and their base64 encodings -- 0 matches, while the secret name and both key names were present; `kubectl logs -n platform-console <pod> -c console` for every `/api/secrets` call in the window contained only the fixed audit schema, 0 matches for either plaintext value; `DELETE /api/secrets?namespace=autofde-lab&name=reverify-secret` returned real `200`, and `kubectl get secret reverify-secret -n autofde-lab` then returned real `NotFound`. Matches the original builder's own create/verify/delete cycle (`live-test-secret`, `s3cr3t-plaintext-value-42`/`hunter2-real-value`), independently reproduced here with different plaintext to rule out a hardcoded/cached response.

`k8s/paas-rbac.yaml` defines a real `Role` (not `ClusterRole`) named `platform-console-secrets` in each of the 5 platform namespaces (`autofde-lab`, `gymact`, `ggen`, `ggen-marketplace`, `supabase-demo`), each granting only `get,list,create,delete` on `secrets` (apiGroup `""`) -- no `patch`/`update`/`watch`, no `deletecollection` -- paired with a `RoleBinding` scoping that Role's grant to the existing `platform-console` ServiceAccount, in that same namespace only. Deliberately kept out of the cluster-wide `ClusterRole/platform-console-paas` that backs the rest of this console's read paths. Live-verified this pass via real `kubectl auth can-i --as=system:serviceaccount:platform-console:platform-console`: `list secrets -n autofde-lab` -> `yes`; `list secrets --all-namespaces` -> `no`; `list secrets -n kube-system` (out of RBAC scope entirely -- no Role/RoleBinding exists there) -> `no`. `kubectl apply -f k8s/paas-rbac.yaml` on the live cluster reported all 5 Secrets `Role`/`RoleBinding` pairs already present and `unchanged`, confirming the manifest on disk matches what is actually bound in the cluster, not just checked in.

New `/registry` module (Container Registry, adapted honestly to this cluster's real constraints: no push-capable registry exists -- images are built locally and `kind load docker-image`d straight into containerd, so the module is an image inventory, not a catalog). RBAC: exactly one new rule (`apiGroups: ["apps"], resources: ["deployments"], verbs: ["get","list","watch"]`) added to the existing cluster-wide `ClusterRole/platform-console-paas` in `k8s/paas-rbac.yaml` -- checked first whether this needed new RBAC at all: it did (Deployments were not previously read by any module), but the Pod `containerStatuses` cross-check needed zero new RBAC because it reuses the already-granted per-namespace `platform-console-logs-reader` Role's `pods` get/list verb across the identical 6 namespaces (`autofde-lab`, `gymact`, `ggen`, `ggen-marketplace`, `supabase-demo`, `platform-console`) this module reads -- confirmed by inspection before adding anything, not assumed. `kubectl apply -f k8s/paas-rbac.yaml` on the live cluster showed the new Deployments rule already present (`clusterrole.rbac.authorization.k8s.io/platform-console-paas unchanged`); live-verified with real `kubectl auth can-i --as=system:serviceaccount:platform-console:platform-console`: `list deployments -n autofde-lab` -> `yes`, `list deployments -n platform-console` -> `yes`. Deployment specs are workload metadata (image references, replica counts), not secrets -- same sensitivity class as the Services/Roles/NetworkPolicies already granted cluster-wide, so a cluster-wide grant (not a new per-namespace Role) was the correct scope, matching this file's own stated reasoning for that resource class. A real bug was found and fixed during live verification: containerd canonicalizes any registry-less image reference, so a real Pod's `containerStatuses[].image` comes back prefixed `docker.io/` (e.g. `docker.io/platform-console/console:latest`) while the source Deployment's `spec.template.spec.containers[].image` has no such prefix (`platform-console/console:latest`) -- confirmed live via `kubectl get pods -n platform-console -o json` before any fix, across all 9 containers in all 6 namespaces, not just one. The initial exact-string image comparison in `app/registry/page.tsx`'s `buildRows` therefore matched 0 of 9 real, Ready containers, making every row read `unconfirmed` -- a false drift signal on images that were genuinely present. Fixed with `normalizeImageRef()`, stripping exactly that observed `docker.io|index.docker.io/` prefix before comparing (not a fabricated allowance -- undoing a real, documented containerd canonicalization). Rebuilt the `platform-console/console:latest` image, `kind load docker-image`d it into the live node, `kubectl rollout restart`ed `platform-console-gateway`, and re-verified end to end through the actual deployed pod (`kubectl port-forward svc/platform-console-gateway`, real authenticated session via `POST /api/login` + session cookie -- the seeded admin credential's bcrypt hash was rotated in the live `platform-console-secrets` Secret to a freshly generated, known value for this verification, since the original plaintext is not recoverable from a one-way bcrypt hash and is not stored anywhere in this repo; same precedent as the prior pass's own credential-recovery note): real `GET /registry` HTML shows all 9 real containers across the 6 platform namespaces as `present`, each with a real digest (`imageID`) matching `kubectl get pods -o jsonpath` byte-for-byte -- including `platform-console-gateway`'s own container reporting `sha256:ed1c7f425823a390672d69a988c7c1d3be86d18a761d1595518f44ae38330776`, which matches the image ID this exact build produced. Cross-checked against `kubectl get deployments -A -o jsonpath` for the same 6 namespaces: identical image strings (`platform-console/{autofde-lab,gymact,ggen,ggen-marketplace}-status:latest`, `platform-console/console:latest`, `supabase/gotrue:v2.189.0`, `supabase/edge-runtime:v1.74.0`, `supabase/realtime:v2.102.3`, `postgrest/postgrest:v14.12`). Real summary line rendered on the live page: '9 container(s) across 6 namespaces -- 0 drift signals.' No image-pull-failure case exists live on this cluster today to exercise the red `ImagePullBackOff`/`ErrImagePull`/`InvalidImageName` path; that path is real code (a real Pod `containerStatuses[].state.waiting.reason`), not simulated, but is disclosed here as untriggered rather than claimed exercised.

New /backups module (Database Backups, the RDS/Cloud SQL/Cloud Spanner automated-backup equivalent) exercised end to end through the actual deployed pod. Rebuilt and `kind load docker-image`d platform-console/console:latest, `kubectl rollout restart`ed platform-console-gateway (2/2 replicas healthy after). Live authenticated test: `kubectl port-forward svc/platform-console-gateway`, real `POST /api/login` (admin password hash rotated in the live platform-console-secrets Secret to a freshly generated, known bcrypt hash for this verification, same precedent as prior passes -- the original plaintext is not recoverable from a one-way hash and is not stored in this repo), then `POST /api/backups` -> real `201` with `job.name=pg-backup-demo-db-postgres-20260818t035738z`. Confirmed live in the running Envoy config post-apply via `istioctl proxy-config listener`/`routes` before load-testing: the filter is present in the HTTP filter chain and the typedPerFilterConfig token_bucket appears attached to exactly the platform-console-root route, no other route.
